teams.synopsis: A dominating Week 3 performance sends this team to the top spot — all positions went for 10+ except the kicker.
teams.blurb: After a dominating performance in Week 3, Max has made his way to the top spot. The team showed no real weaknesses this week, having all positions go for 10+, except for <mark class="hl-player">Fairbairn</mark>. My biggest question mark is with this team's number of touchdowns — it's tricky to project touchdowns, but through 3 weeks <mark class="hl-player">Nabers</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Barkley</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Henry</mark> have combined for 12 TDs. This most likely will change, but I wouldn't be shocked if it doesn't. Also, the bench depth is interesting to note for future trades.

teams.synopsis: Back in the top 2 after a brief stint at 3rd — 137 points for the second time in three weeks.
teams.blurb: Making his way back into the top 2 after a short stint in the 3rd spot. Aidan's team was able to put up 137 points for the 2nd time in three weeks, solidifying himself with a top roster. On the surface level, you may say the team has only one competent running back, but when <mark class="hl-player">Joe Mixon</mark> is healthy, this team will have borderline top-10 players at each position in the starting lineup.

teams.synopsis: Drops from 1st for the first time since preseason, but still put up 126 without CMC and Deebo.
teams.blurb: Taking a little bit of a step back in the rankings, Root's team drops from 1st for the first time since preseason. Although the team was still able to put up 126 points despite not having <mark class="hl-player">CMC</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Deebo</mark>, over a third of the points came from a career game by <mark class="hl-player">Jauan Jennings</mark>. This team has all the tools to be top 3 rest of season, but if <mark class="hl-player">Andrews</mark> isn't going to average at least 10 points, then this team might have a tight end problem that limits its ability to contend with the other elite teams.

teams.synopsis: At 4th for the second straight week — the 'elite' label stands, but the running back situation in Tampa is worth watching.
teams.blurb: Despite a loss to Charlie in Week 3, Brandon finds his team at 4th on the rankings for the second straight week. Last week I put the 'elite' label on this team, and I'm not taking it away, but it may just be a great team. On the positive side, <mark class="hl-player">Jefferson</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Metcalf</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Montgomery</mark> seem like top-15 players at their positions, while <mark class="hl-player">Lamar</mark> is proving worthy of a 4th-round pick. However, it may be important to note how the running back situation unfolds in Tampa.

teams.synopsis: One of the biggest risers this week, jumping from 9 to 5, as the WR corps finally got it going.
teams.blurb: One of the biggest risers in the rankings this week, and for good reason, jumping from 9 to 5. The wide receivers finally got it going, with <mark class="hl-player">Rashee</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Cooper</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Terry</mark> combining for 76.7 points in Week 3. Solid quarterback and running back play will be there weekly for the team, but the tight end production might be a little concerning from <mark class="hl-player">LaPorta</mark> right now. I wouldn't be shocked if this team takes over a top-4 spot next week.

teams.synopsis: 0-3 but still moving up to 6th — the RB2 and flex remain the real weaknesses on an otherwise loaded roster.
teams.blurb: This is going to be a hot take, and I'm okay with that. Despite Deniz's team being 0-3, they find themselves moving up the rankings to the 6th spot. I believe Week 4 will bring this team's breakout performance, with players like <mark class="hl-player">Stroud</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Collins</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Moore</mark>, while <mark class="hl-player">Bijan</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Ferguson</mark> hold down the RB1 and TE positions. The weaknesses on this team are big, however, and may be the cause of FKP's downfall — the RB2 and flex.

teams.synopsis: Moving back up to 7th despite no Kupp or Brown — the Andy Dalton-led Panthers may make two more names relevant.
teams.blurb: Shockingly, my team is moving back up the rankings to 7th this week despite not having <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark> or <mark class="hl-player">Brown</mark>. The Andy Dalton-led Panthers look like they may just make <mark class="hl-player">Hubbard</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Diontae</mark> fantasy relevant, but it's still only been one week. There are definitely darker days ahead for this team, but if it can just stay afloat until those fantasy stars come back, then a weekly top-7 ranking doesn't seem so far out of reach.

teams.synopsis: Chase finally showed up with 29.8, propelling a Monday night win — settling into that 7-10 bubble range.
teams.blurb: I believe GOC is starting to settle into a range within the rankings, that 7-10 range where the bubble playoff teams are. <mark class="hl-player">Ja'Marr Chase</mark> finally showed up for Cole in Week 3, dropping 29.8 points, which propelled him to a win on Monday night against FKP. For the rest of the team, <mark class="hl-player">Sutton</mark> could be a solid flex and the running backs can both put up 15+ weekly, but <mark class="hl-player">Pittman Jr.</mark> might be a trade candidate if Cole wants to shake things up.

teams.synopsis: Two straight sub-100 weeks, falling from 4 to 7 to 9 — QB and TE play is the culprit.
teams.blurb: Two straight weeks of failing to reach 100 points is not how you want to start the season, which has caused the team to fall from 4 to 7 to 9. This fall can be attributed to poor quarterback and tight end play, while the wide receivers and running backs haven't been consistent enough to put together a great week. However, I expect the team to bounce back in the coming weeks and get back into the top half of the rankings.

teams.synopsis: 76 points in Week 3 drops him back to 10th after two weeks at 5 — Darnold and Breece are the lone positives for now.
teams.blurb: A really bad performance in Week 3 (76 points) causes Anthony to drop back down to the 10th spot after spending two weeks at 5. The positives are that <mark class="hl-player">Darnold</mark> might be a playable weekly quarterback, <mark class="hl-player">Breece</mark> will be a top-5 running back rest of season, and... that's about it for now. Poor games from the rest of the starting lineup led to the low point total, but the biggest concern comes from <mark class="hl-player">Waddle</mark>.

teams.synopsis: Dropped a very good 126 points in Week 3 — the Taylor/Kyren duo looks like one of the best in the league.
teams.blurb: Dropping a very good 126 points in Week 3, this team is beginning its ascent back to the upper half of the rankings. The running back duo of <mark class="hl-player">Taylor</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Kyren</mark> is proving to be one of the best in the league, both top-10 players at the position. <mark class="hl-player">Jayden Daniels</mark> is another positive spot on this roster, but besides him the rest is mostly disappointing, particularly the wide receiver and tight end positions.

teams.synopsis: A rollercoaster of emotions — hasn't been within the same 4 spots in consecutive weeks yet.
teams.blurb: A rollercoaster of emotions is what this team is — I haven't ranked Quin within the same 4 spots in consecutive weeks yet, so expect anything to happen in Week 4. Not much to say about the Week 3 performance, except that <mark class="hl-player">Mayfield</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Shaheed</mark> may be frauds, and the rest of his running backs and wide receivers may have lower floors than expected.

teams.synopsis: Debating dropping this to 14th, but a glimpse of WR-trio life keeps hope for a mid-season comeback alive.
teams.blurb: I was debating placing Carmine's team back into the 14th spot this week because of the poor performance, but I still see some hope for a mid-season comeback. Like Ben's team, this one is relying on its wide receiver trio to produce big numbers, and this week we may have seen a glimpse of that. There's no way to sugarcoat it — this team needs to make a trade to boost its running backs.

teams.synopsis: 0-3 with sub-100 every week — the WR trio hasn't come close to carrying this team yet.
teams.blurb: A sad 0-3 start to the season leads to Ben being placed at 14th for the 2nd week in a row. Hasn't scored at least 100 points in a week yet. The wide receiver trio of <mark class="hl-player">Hill</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">London</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> was supposed to carry this team through thick and thin, but Hill may be a borderline WR2 with no <mark class="hl-player">Tua</mark>, Aiyuk can't capitalize on a depleted 49ers offense, and London has been inconsistent but had a good Week 3.
